toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B most likely had a one-off potassium QC outlier. It was not a fault in the analyzer or the new reagent lot. Evidence: the repeat of the same vial passed 21 minutes later. Levels 1 and 3 were normal. Level 2 averaged 5.80 after the lot change versus 5.81 before. All 182 scheduled QC runs were completed, so the short-staffing theory doesn't hold. Twenty-three held samples and a random 20 of the 186 flagged results agreed with Analyzer A to within 0.02 mmol/L on average. The patient median is unchanged. A single 1-3s flag is expected about once or twice a month by chance. A transient sampling glitch is possible, but nobody can confirm it, so don't record it as the cause.

Ward 6 highs are split evenly between Analyzers A and B (7 each). They line up with the tube outage (long transport times) and four renal overflow patients. That fits delayed transport better than analyzer error, though this is not proven.

What to sign off: return Analyzer B potassium to service and close the review of the flagged results without amendments. Add a temporary extra Level 2 QC per shift for a week. Do not recall all results, quarantine the lot or widen limits. Ask Ward 6 for fresh repeat samples and fix the tube station.
output.methodChoice: No further evidence collected; initial evidence was sufficient to discriminate.
